requirements.evidence: The contract is implemented: migrations with cascading FKs, the unique (queue_id, code) constraint and the recommended index (create_tickets_table.php:16-27); Queue and Ticket models with the required casts and relations (Queue.php:11-37, Ticket.php:61-80); Entity::queues() (Entity.php:46); both enums; InactiveQueueException extends RuntimeException; IssueTicket rejects negative priority (IssueTicket.php:30), locks the queue row and re-reads is_active (IssueTicket.php:54-58), and retries on code conflicts (IssueTicket.php:36-46). nextCode follows insertion order and skips malformed codes via lazyByIdDesc plus '/^A(\d+)$/D' (Ticket.php:86-97). Write-once uses an updating hook (Ticket.php:33-46). call() authorizes through a policy and re-reads the row under lock (Ticket.php:105-123). Factories have forQueue and keep an explicit code. Deviation: because nextCode is derived from the last surviving row, deleting the most recent ticket makes its number available again, and docs/business-rules.md:545 says so. The task says deleting a ticket does not reuse its number.

conventions.evidence: Issuance is an invokable Action (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php). Calling is authorized through a new policy, TicketPolicy::call, invoked with Gate::forUser(...)->authorize (Ticket.php:107). Migrations have generated timestamps and reversible down(). Fillable is set explicitly with the #[Fillable] attribute on both models. docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md and CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] are updated. Public methods have PHPDoc. call() lives on the model because the task contract requires it there.

security.evidence: Ticket::call checks membership server-side through a policy before any write (Ticket.php:107, TicketPolicy.php:13-16), and an outsider leaves the ticket unchanged. The call is re-checked under lockForUpdate to prevent double calls (Ticket.php:111-115). Fillable lists are deliberate; called_at and called_by_user_id are not mass-assignable. The task defines no user for issuance, so IssueTicket has nothing to authorize. No HTTP or Livewire surface.

tests.evidence: Four Pest files cover: defaults, enum persistence, sequencing, negative priority, inactive and stale-inactive queues, collision retry and bounded give-up (IssueTicketTest.php); all nextCode examples from the task (NextCodeTest.php); write-once with a dataset and the call-field allowance (TicketWriteOnceTest.php); member, outsider, other-entity, double-call and stale-instance calls (CallTicketTest.php); cascade and slug uniqueness (QueueTest.php). Gaps: TicketWriteOnceTest.php:1031-1035 passes called_at and called_by_user_id to update(), but they are not fillable, so they are silently dropped and only status is checked. No test covers deleting the latest ticket or factory count() usage.

simplicity.evidence: The code is lean overall: one action, one policy, and a model hook for write-once. nextCode's lazyByIdDesc()->map()->first() is a compact way to skip malformed codes in insertion order. isCodeConflict matches on message strings ('tickets.code' / 'tickets_queue_code_unique', IssueTicket.php:71-77), which is driver-dependent and somewhat brittle. The retry loop with $ticket = null and a break is slightly roundabout.

readability.evidence: Names are clear (CALL_FIELDS, CODE_PATTERN, numberOf, isCodeConflict), methods are small, and the short comments explain why ("The caller's instance may be stale: read is_active from the locked row", "Re-read under lock: this instance may be stale"). Style matches the Laravel siblings. No dead code or debugging output.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task. TicketPolicy supports the required authorization for calling. The doc edits are limited to the queue and ticket sections and the schema notes. There is no call-next selection, UI or totem API.

issues.explanation: nextCode derives the next number from the last surviving valid row, so deleting the most recent ticket (e.g. A003 after A001..A003) makes the next code A003 again; the task says deleting a ticket does not reuse its number, and the docs record this deviation instead of fixing it.
update() is passed called_at and called_by_user_id, which are not in $fillable, so they are silently discarded and the test only proves that status may change, not that the call fields may.

The code is allocated in afterMaking, and count(n)->create() makes every instance before persisting any of them, so Ticket::factory()->count(2)->forQueue($q)->create() gives both tickets A001 and hits the unique constraint.

Detecting the unique violation by substring-matching the driver error message is brittle; checking a UniqueConstraintViolationException (available in recent Laravel) or the SQLSTATE code would be more robust.

review.summary: The change adds the queues and tickets schema, the Queue and Ticket models, enums, factories, a TicketPolicy and the IssueTicket action, with locked re-reads, collision retry, write-once enforcement, single-call authorization, solid Pest coverage and updated docs. The main deviation is that deleting the most recent ticket lets its code be reused, which contradicts the 'never reuse' rule, though the change documents it openly. A weak write-once test and a factory count() edge case are smaller issues. I would approve after these are addressed.
